chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: A musician's marriage and his wife's career
summary: He reflects on the strain of musician life on a wife; she became a caterer and kept apart from the music world.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: And her sister. And that's how we met. And she's a wonderful woman. You know it's very difficult for a woman to be understanding in this life of a musician because it's a hard life, you see what I mean, up to a point. While it's glamorous and you're workin' and everything's goin' well, but when things fail, then this is where the other stuff comes in. A person that works nine to five on a job for years and years and years is different, you know. And so we had to come to an understanding about a lot of things, a lot of heartbreak and suffering and etcetera which I'm sure all musicians go through, you know, in their married life.
When you came to New York did she continue her interest and work with antiques?
Yeah, she did jobs and then I sent her to school and she became a cateress. And so she's been busy all through the years. She stuck with what she loves...
And never really had very much
to do with the music world?

No, not really, you know, she took care of me; she's a good cook and took care of the home and she worked, you know what I mean, so I mean my world was a different world. But we had an understanding when I got home, you know what I mean, we had a different life, you know, at home.
